message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower isn’t a quick weekend job – it’s a multi‑year project even under ideal conditions. Here’s why:

| Factor | Typical Value | Impact on Timeline |
|--------|---------------|--------------------|
| **Surface area** | ≈ 140 000 m² (≈ 1.5 million ft²) | More area → more paint & labor |
| **Crew productivity** | A skilled painter can cover ~ 30–50 m² per day (including prep, drying, safety checks) | With a single crew of 20–30 people, you’d finish ~ 600–900 m² per week |
| **Work schedule** | 8‑hour shifts, 5 days a week (weather‑dependent) | Continuous work would take ~ 200–250 weeks (~ 4 years) |
| **Logistics & safety** | Scaffold erection/maintenance, crane operations, permits, nighttime work restrictions | Adds downtime; realistic pace drops to ~ 100–150 m² per week |

### Rough Estimate

* **Continuous, full‑time effort** (no breaks, all‑weather): ~ 4 years  
* **Realistic, phased approach** (scaffold changes, weather windows, safety inspections): ~ 5–10 years

So, if you were to start painting today and worked nonstop, you’d finish in roughly **four years**. In practice, accounting for safety, logistics, and weather, most estimates put the project at **five to ten years**.
